title: Writing by hand is good for your brain
author: dwwoelfel
relevanceReason: 命中 1 个 AI/科技关键词。

comments.author: dhosek
comments.textRawHtml:
On the gadget front, I really love the paperlike screen protector for the iPad. This combined with the Apple Pencil made a huge difference in the usability of my iPad for writing/drawing. I still prefer to write on paper, but it’s really great for things like my writing group where we generally meet over zoom & I can give the author a marked up manuscript (with multicolor notes).

I’m also opposed to getting too precious about writing tools. So many people have drawers full of fancy notebooks with something on the first few pages and the rest empty. Get something and use it. Don’t matter if it’s a dollar-store spiral notebook or a fancy Leuchturm 1917 notebook, just as long as you use it. Same with the writing utensil. Pencil? Ballpoint pen? Whatever. I find these days I prefer to write using a cheap mechanical pencil (the kind they sell in bags of 20 at the supermarket), but I’ll use whatever.

I used to be really precious about these things. I only used college-ruled 9½×6 150-page spiral bound notebooks and wrote in 0.4mm fine-point felt tip pen. Did all my first drafts by hand. It ended up being an excuse to not finish stuff. I do most of my first drafts typing now, because it lets me get s⸻ done (although I still take notes by hand because that helps me remember what I took notes on better).

I don’t buy the cursive thing, mostly because I write slower in cursive than in print (although I have a handful of ligatures and abbreviations I use to speed up some things).
comments.textZhHtml:
在小工具方面，我非常喜欢 iPad 的纸质屏幕保护膜。与 Apple Pencil 相结合，我的 iPad 书写/绘图的可用性发生了巨大变化。我仍然更喜欢在纸上写作，但这对于像我的写作小组这样的事情来说真的很棒，我们通常在变焦上见面，而且我可以给作者一份标记的手稿（带有彩色注释）。

我也反对过于珍惜书写工具。很多人的抽屉里都装满了精美的笔记本，前几页上写着一些东西，其余的都是空的。得到一些东西并使用它。无论是一元店的螺旋笔记本还是精美的 Leuchturm 1917 笔记本，只要您使用它即可。与书写用具相同。铅笔？圆珠笔？任何。我发现现在我更喜欢用便宜的自动铅笔（超市里卖的 20 支一袋的那种）写字，但我会用任何东西。

我曾经非常珍惜这些东西。我只使用大学用的 9½×6 150 页螺旋装订笔记本，并用 0.4 毫米细尖毡尖笔书写。我所有的初稿都是手工完成的。这最终成为了没有完成任务的借口。我现在大部分初稿都是打字，因为它可以让我完成（尽管我仍然用手记笔记，因为这可以帮助我更好地记住我记下的内容）。

我不买草书，主要是因为我用草书写得比印刷体慢（尽管我有一些连字和缩写，可以用来加快某些事情的速度）。

children.author: ksenzee
children.textRawHtml: The cursive thing is almost certainly because he's using fountain pens. Pencils and ballpoint pens lend themselves to printing more easily, because they require pressure to write, and when you let the pressure up between letters, the line stops. The first time I picked up a fountain pen and tried printing with it, I found all my letters were connecting whether I meant them to or not, and I suddenly understood why cursive exists. Everyone who's learned cursive in the ballpoint pen era has been unwittingly taught a performance optimization for a tool they're not using.
children.textZhHtml: 草书几乎可以肯定是因为他使用钢笔。铅笔和圆珠笔更容易打印，因为它们需要压力才能书写，当你在字母之间加大压力时，线条就会停止。当我第一次拿起钢笔尝试用它打印时，我发现我所有的字母都在连接，无论我是否有意，我突然明白了为什么存在草书。每个在圆珠笔时代学过草书的人都在不知不觉中学会了对他们不使用的工具进行性能优化。

children.textRawHtml: Wow I never knew this - what a useful bit of information. Makes me want to try a fountain pen, I do like writing in cursive but I often get hand cramps doing it for extended periods.
children.textZhHtml: 哇，我从来不知道这个 - 多么有用的信息。让我想尝试一下钢笔，我确实喜欢用草书写字，但长时间写字我经常会手抽筋。

children.author: nyrikki
children.textRawHtml:
From the OP:

> "I learned cursive as a child. Then I went for many years without using it much, and forgot some of it."

While fountain pens may be nicer for cursive, they were very late in the games only coming into the scene in the late 1800s, long after fashion had been set.

In the US we were taught either the Zaner-Bloser or the D'Nealian alphabet, and while most of the claims of cursive over manuscript are typically overblown and fall under scrutiny, with common use it may not be faster, but is easer for (the small sample of friends I have asked) to write while not looking at the paper. Not faster, but easier to write in strait lines without looking (in my experience).

Manuscript (now called printing) wasn't common when Zaner-Bloser printed the book "The arm movement method of rapid writing"[0] IIRC.

But for business writing (which both Zaner-Bloser and D'Nealian were targeting) it is not so much the fact that you aren't lifting the point, but that you are using your whole arm.

The scientific claims of Zaner-Bloser are almost certainly suspect, but before word-processors, taking notes while not watching your writing was a critical skill, or was in my experience.

That is a very different world that the scribes of old, or even Roman cursive, which would have only had quills, and which did not really connect letters.

If you look into secretary hand, italic hand, and court hand, a lot of it had to to with style and preferences, with the US Declaration of Independence being in Secretary Hand, which had been in fashion for official docs for centuries at that point. Shakespeare also wrote his plays Secretary Hand, while ladies of the era would have used 'Italian style' italics.

So unfortunately it seems there are many back explanations, the real history is clear as mud in the absence of direct evidence, or more correctly, claims like in Zaner-Bloser.

[0] https://archive.org/details/armmovementmetho00zane/page/n3/m...
children.textZhHtml:
来自OP：

> “我小时候学过草书。后来我很多年都没有怎么用它，并且忘记了一些。”

虽然钢笔可能更适合草写，但它们在游戏中出现的时间很晚，直到 1800 年代末才出现，那时时尚已经定型很久了。

在美国，我们要么被教 Zaner-Bloser，要么被教 D'Nealian 字母表，虽然大多数关于草书优于手稿的说法通常都被夸大了，并且受到审查，但在普遍使用的情况下，它可能不会更快，但更容易（我问过的一小部分朋友）在不看论文的情况下写作。 不是更快，而是更容易在不看的情况下用直线书写（根据我的经验）。

当 Zaner-Bloser 印刷《快速书写的手臂运动方法》一书[0] IIRC 时，手稿（现在称为印刷）并不常见。

但对于商业写作（Zaner-Bloser 和 D'Nealian 的目标）来说，并不是你没有提出要点，而是你在使用你的整个手臂。

赞纳-布洛瑟的科学主张几乎肯定是值得怀疑的，但在文字处理器出现之前，在不看自己的写作的情况下做笔记是一项关键技能，或者根据我的经验。

这是一个非常不同的世界，与古代的抄写员甚至罗马草书相比，后者只有羽毛笔，并且没有真正连接字母。

如果你研究秘书手、斜体手和宫廷手，很多都与风格和偏好有关，美国《独立宣言》是用秘书手写的，当时这在官方文件中已经流行了几个世纪。莎士比亚还写了他的戏剧《秘书汉德》，而那个时代的女士们会使用“意大利风格”斜体。

不幸的是，似乎有很多背后的解释，在没有直接证据的情况下，真正的历史就像泥巴一样清晰，或者更准确地说，没有像赞纳-布洛瑟那样的说法。

[0] https://archive.org/details/armmovementmetho00zane/page/n3/m...

children.author: ksenzee
children.textRawHtml:
To clarify my point, I am fairly sure the issue is not fountain pens requiring less pressure to write with than everything else, but rather ballpoint pens requiring more pressure than all earlier pen technology. I have not used a dip pen myself, but I can't imagine it would require pressure to write.

In other words, all of the writing tools in common use since ~1950 make it easy to separate your letters, but before the ballpoint pen became commonplace, every writer had had the experience of using a pen that makes connecting letters easier than separating them. That's the experience most of us today are missing.
children.textZhHtml:
为了澄清我的观点，我相当确定问题不是钢笔比其他笔需要更少的压力来书写，而是圆珠笔比所有早期的笔技术需要更大的压力。我自己没有用过蘸水笔，但我无法想象它会需要压力来书写。

换句话说，自 1950 年以来所有常用的书写工具都可以轻松地将字母分开，但在圆珠笔普及之前，每个作家都有过使用笔的经验，这种笔使连接字母比分开字母更容易。这是我们今天大多数人所缺少的经历。

children.author: ricardobayes
children.textRawHtml: Not a sarcastic response, instead, to double down on your point. If you show this to 99.9% of the world and require the spend of $50 for the screen protector on the $500 iPad to get the "paper feel", they will tell you might as well just get that Leuchtturm or Moleskin notebook.
children.textZhHtml: 不是讽刺性的回应，而是强调你的观点。如果您向世界上 99.9% 的人展示此产品，并需要花费 50 美元为 500 美元的 iPad 购买屏幕保护膜以获得“纸质感觉”，他们会告诉您不妨购买 Leuchtturm 或 Moleskin 笔记本。

children.author: RandomWorker
children.textRawHtml: That’s what kept me from going iPad. At the price of a 1000 setup you can buy about 25 Moleskins  with, 280 pages each, + pens. If you fill 10 pages a day, that’s two years of high quality paper. My rate is more like 3-4 pages a day. So, I’m just so far out. My sense is that an iPad would last 3-4 years then it needs a battery replacement.
children.textZhHtml: 这就是我放弃使用 iPad 的原因。以 1000 个套装的价格，您可以购买大约 25 个 Moleskins，每个 Moleskins 280 页，+ 笔。如果每天写 10 页，就相当于两年的高质量纸张。我的速度是每天 3-4 页。所以，我还很遥远。我的感觉是，iPad 可以使用 3-4 年，然后就需要更换电池。

children.author: itsdavesanders
children.textRawHtml:
Yes but you can’t watch Netflix on a Moleskin.

If all you’re doing is writing then it’s not worth it, but for me the iPad is a fantastic piece of kit that can consume media, create media, and of all types, writing to fully mastered music albums.
children.textZhHtml:
是的，但你不能在 Moleskin 上观看 Netflix。

如果你所做的只是写作，那就不值得了，但对我来说，iPad 是一个很棒的工具包，可以使用媒体、创建媒体以及所有类型的内容，写入完全掌握的音乐专辑。

children.author: bigyabai
children.textRawHtml:
Most people I know that make music on an iPad only use it for specific plugins or MIDI apps. They bounce the stems out to WAV and then mix/master it in a full desktop DAW.

You'd go through a lot of unnecessary suffering trying to do a professional mixdown and master on iPad.
children.textZhHtml:
据我所知，大多数在 iPad 上制作音乐的人仅将其用于特定插件或 MIDI 应用程序。他们将主干弹跳到 WAV，然后在完整的桌面 DAW 中对其进行混音/母带处理。

尝试在 iPad 上进行专业混音和母带处理会经历很多不必要的痛苦。

children.author: yurimo
children.textRawHtml: Personally found newest paperlike to be a lot like glass still, you barely get that paper feel at all and I hated it. They tried to keep clarity of the screen near glass level, but that affects the feeling a lot. Eventually I did some research and found that Japanese screen protectors that give you a feel of Kent paper are excellent for writing, so I wholeheartedly recommend those. You can find best rated ones by looking at top rated ones on jp websites, I have bellemond one.
children.textZhHtml: 个人发现最新的纸状材料仍然很像玻璃，你几乎没有那种纸质的感觉，我讨厌它。他们试图将屏幕的清晰度保持在接近玻璃水平，但这对感觉影响很大。最终我做了一些研究，发现日本的屏幕保护膜给你一种肯特纸的感觉，非常适合书写，所以我全心推荐这些。您可以通过查看日本网站上评分最高的内容来找到评分最高的内容，我有一个 Bellemond。

children.author: killerstorm
children.textRawHtml:
I used ballpoint pens in school but I don't like the process: my hand often feels too tense, and getting handwriting legible is a lot of effort. Once I switched to fountain pens I enjoy the process a lot more, and the result generally look better without much effort.

I'm sure many people are OK with ballpoint pens and might even prefer the feel.

Fountain pen (+ ink and paper) doesn't really cost more than a paperlike screen protector. So it can be entirely functional. But many people also enjoy it as a hobby, collecting pens and whatnot.
children.textZhHtml:
我在学校使用圆珠笔，但我不喜欢这个过程：我的手经常感觉太紧张，而且要让笔迹清晰可辨需要很大的努力。一旦我改用钢笔，我就更喜欢这个过程，而且结果通常看起来更好，而且不需要太多努力。

我确信很多人都可以使用圆珠笔，甚至可能更喜欢这种感觉。

钢笔（+墨水和纸张）实际上并不比纸质屏幕保护膜贵。所以它可以是完全实用的。但许多人也将其作为一种爱好，收集钢笔之类的。

children.author: annzabelle
children.textRawHtml: I think you're right. It's very easy in any hobby to make the gear side of the hobby be disproportionate to how much you actually do the hobby. Think someone who's spent $3k on camping gear and constantly researches gear, but rarely camps. On the other hand, if you do actually camp a lot, it is nice to have the lighter weight higher performance gear, up to a certain point. So, Stephenson, as someone who does actually write a massive amount, is right to be using high performance gear, but for someone just getting started, getting into fancy pens/paper is a distraction from actually writing.
children.textZhHtml: 我认为你是对的。在任何爱好中，很容易使爱好的齿轮部分与您实际从事该爱好的程度不成比例。想象一下有人花了 3000 美元购买露营装备并不断研究装备，但很少露营。另一方面，如果您确实经常露营，那么在某种程度上，拥有重量更轻、性能更高的装备是很好的。因此，斯蒂芬森作为一个确实进行大量写作的人，使用高性能设备是正确的，但对于刚刚开始的人来说，使用精美的笔/纸会分散实际写作的注意力。

children.author: galangalalgol
children.textRawHtml: If you are writing a lot and have dysgraphia, a cheap fountain pen like pilot varsity ($2) or platinum preppy ($7) can help you fight the excessive pressure we tend to use leading to less hand cramping. Using tools that make you write more because it is more enjoyable is good, using tools that make you spend time thinking about tools is bad. I really liked those tiny comp pads cvs sold, but I haven't seen them in a while and I don't like the dollar store ones. I just grab random pads that aren't bigger than my phone so they sit nice in my pocket.
children.textZhHtml: 如果您经常写字并且患有书写困难，那么一支便宜的钢笔，例如 Pilot varsity（2 美元）或 Platinum Preppy（7 美元）可以帮助您对抗我们通常使用的过度压力，从而减少手抽筋。使用让你写得更多、因为更有趣的工具是好的，使用让你花时间思考工具的工具是坏的。我真的很喜欢 cvs 出售的那些小型补偿垫，但我已经有一段时间没有看到它们了，而且我不喜欢一元店的垫子。我只是随机抓起一些不比手机大的垫子，这样它们就可以很好地放在我的口袋里。

children.author: runtime_lens
children.textRawHtml: I think people send too much time optimizing the notebook instead of optimizing what goes into it. I've seen beautifully organized notebooks that were never opened again and messy scraps of paper that someone referred back to after years.
children.textZhHtml: 我认为人们花费了太多时间来优化笔记本，而不是优化其中的内容。我见过组织精美但再也没有打开过的笔记本，也见过多年后有人回想起的凌乱的纸片。

children.author: carlmr
children.textRawHtml:
> I find these days I prefer to write using a cheap mechanical pencil

I know this is contrary to your advice but mechanical pencil, get a Kuru Toga, it's a really nice improvement and not very expensive. It auto-rotates the pencil tip, so you don't have the sharp end at some point.

For permanent writing get a Uni ball gel writer, it's supremely smooth to write with. Also not hugely expensive.

They're both not the cheapest option, but an amazing writing experience without being the fancy kind of expensive.
children.textZhHtml:
> 我发现这些天我更喜欢用便宜的自动铅笔写字

我知道这与你的建议相反，但是自动铅笔，买一支 Kuru Toga，这是一个非常好的改进，而且不是很贵。它会自动旋转铅笔尖，因此您在某些时候不会有锋利的末端。

要进行永久书写，请使用 Uni 球形凝胶书写器，书写起来非常顺畅。也不是很贵。

它们都不是最便宜的选择，但却是一种令人惊叹的写作体验，而且价格也不是那么昂贵。

children.author: setopt
children.textRawHtml: Paperlike is indeed nice for handwriting, but it has drawbacks. The increased friction makes it uncomfortable to use your fingers to navigate the iPad for long, and since it makes the finger motion along the screen less smooth, it sometimes prevents the iPad from correctly interpreting drag-and-drop or multi-finger gestures in my experience. It also makes writing very noisy compared to the stock iPad, and also compared to paper, so if you have a shared office you might want to reconsider. I ended up removing it again from my iPad. But to be fair, this was on a $400 iPad ~5 years ago, so perhaps high-end iPads with newer Paperlike versions work better.
children.textZhHtml: Paperlike确实很适合手写，但它也有缺点。增加的摩擦力使长时间使用手指操作 iPad 变得不舒服，并且由于它使手指在屏幕上的运动不太顺畅，根据我的经验，有时会阻止 iPad 正确解释拖放或多指手势。与普通 iPad 相比，与纸张相比，它还使得书写变得非常嘈杂，因此，如果您有共用办公室，您可能需要重新考虑。我最终又把它从 iPad 上删除了。但公平地说，这是大约 5 年前在 400 美元的 iPad 上进行的，因此也许具有较新 Paperlike 版本的高端 iPad 效果更好。
